summary: loader-diag-xnu-sa-md1 ran once on the S24 (decision 0035, RECOVERY only, restored from the pinned stock, Android checked) and did NOT reach its question: the root delivery stopped at the 225 s cap with 2,273,312,768 of 2,475,720,704 bytes (91.82%) at 10.10 MB/s (NAT-078/083/085/087 delivered the whole root at 15.0-17.1 MB/s in 145-165 s), the kernel then booted on a root whose last 202,407,936 bytes were never written; the Stage A small root (md0) mounted and showed all 20 plists, init passed 35 of 35 checks, but /bin/df, /sbin/mount, /bin/ps and /sbin/launchd.darwin failed with `Input/output error` (exit 127), vm_stat was killed by signal 9, init finished and the kernel shut down at kernel time 276.54 s. Chain row 7 (not fully delivered: the launchd stage is not evaluated); Stage A ladder row A8 (no launchd line). No Apple daemon was started; the question of decision 0035 is unanswered.

acceptance.1_run_and_restore: One run under decision 0035 (committed 7630d56 before the launch): RECOVERY written once (reboot requested 2026-11-12T16:29:22.914Z), loader appeared +18.5 s, the loader's 360 s deadline returned the phone to Download Mode (`SAMSUNG USB`, +379.5 s on the watcher's clock), NAT-013 restore with the pyusb venv python, `assess` pass (pit validated, upload acknowledged, session end confirmed, reboot confirmed, android booted, recovery readback matches), check_android: SM-S921B/e1s/S921BXXS9BYH3, boot_completed 1, user data directories present, RECOVERY hash equals the pinned stock. No retry of this image: the one-shot marker exists. A first launch at 16:02:48Z stopped at the driver's adb check before any write (phone left the USB bus; report.json device_write_started false, reboot_sent false) and did not consume the attempt.
acceptance.2_analysers: analyze_nat087.py and analyze_nat089.py were run unchanged after the collector and watcher exited: chain row 7 and Stage A row A8 (not-evaluated: no launchd line). The tables of both are empty: no launchd line exists.
acceptance.3_row_other_than_A1: Recorded as the finding, task NOT completed (a non-pass outcome).

findings: Delivery shortfall: 2,273,312,768 B in 225.1 s = 10.10 MB/s (the loader's receive cap is 240 s). The rate was flat at 9.2-10.7 MB/s from the first seconds, so it is not a stall; rx errors, aborts, resets, gaps were all 0. At the 15-17 MB/s of the four earlier runs the whole root needs 145-165 s. The host was heavily loaded (at 16:42Z, after the run: load average 30.5 / 28.5 / 21.0 over 1 / 5 / 15 min on 12 cores): three leaked mutant-test processes of MY OWN earlier NAT-089 mutation pass (killed at 16:42Z after this run was analysed; they had run for 69-70 minutes at ~95% CPU each, i.e. during the whole run) plus the owner's Java/gradle work. That the load caused the rate drop is a likely explanation, not a measurement.

The kernel did not wait for or check the missing tail: it booted at the cap and mounted the APFS root (md1) with the delivered 91.82% in place; the first four rc programs and launchd.darwin read as `Input/output error`, which is consistent with their data lying in the undelivered tail but was not checked against the image's extent map.

New positive observation: the 4 MiB Stage A small root (md0) built by NAT-089 is mounted by the S24 kernel and lists all 20 plists (19 Apple + com.nat085.ps) under /redwood/LaunchDaemons, with the sizes of the host files: the APFS container of NAT-089 holds the plists (NAT-090 could not tie them to the container by a byte search).

The transport worked: 1 boot, 455 frames, 453 records, 0 drops, 0 faults, 0 stalls, dump why=2 of 24,315 bytes (head 8,192 + tail 16,123, gap 0, closed): all of the kernel's text from init up to CPU halted.
established: The run happened as described and the phone is back on the stock RECOVERY with Android and user data intact.
A root delivered to 91.82% does not boot launchd: a delivered-bytes check is needed before the kernel starts (the loader proceeded at the cap).
The Stage A small root mounts and holds the plists on the S24.
not_established: Anything about Apple daemons under restore-mode launchd: launchd was never executed.
That the load on the host caused the slower delivery; that the five failing files lie in the undelivered tail.
Whether a complete delivery at 15 MB/s would have run the same chain as NAT-088 (it is expected, not shown).
disclosures: adb: the first `adb devices` of this session hung (server start in the agent shell); a server was started with `setsid nohup adb nodaemon server`.

Leaked processes of my own NAT-089 first mutation pass (3 mutants stuck in loops) ran during this run; found only after the delivery cap was reached; not detected earlier because the pass had been stopped by killing its parent.
Restore used NAT-013's restore_stock.py (not the driver's --restore), as the protocol of decision 0035 states.
The NAT-089/090 evidence files carry recorded_at times that are local time labelled UTC (see docs/procedures/nat-090/ERRATA.md).
